title: Slabbed GPU memory budgeting: weights / KV / activations headroom plan
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: define and implement a slab-based GPU memory budgeting system that explicitly divides device memory into weight, KV cache, and activation/working slabs with dynamic headroom reservations to reduce OOMs and tail latency under continuous batching. This ticket covers design decisions, prototype allocator, telemetry, and a staged rollout plan for Dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by infra and runtime teams
Prototype allocator implemented in dev branch and gated behind feature flag
Benchmarks show <=5% average latency regression and >=25% reduction in OOMs on mixed single-tenant workloads compared to current baseline
Per-tenant memory accounting and alerting surfaced in Console (token-level/route-level breakdown) for experiment clusters
Rollout runbook and fallback path documented (feature flag off -> revert without needing restart)
comments: 2026-02-15 - Aisha Raman: Kickoff — initial problem statement collected from incident INC-2026-011 where mixed long-context chat + batched reranking caused KV pressure cascading to OOMs. Hypothesis: unbounded KV growth + bursty activation footprints with current best-effort allocator leads to headroom starvation. Proposal: slab allocator + soft-reservations for headroom per tenant/queue.

2026-02-20 - Connor Blake: Added measurement plan — capture distribution of (weights, kv_bytes, peak_activations) per model and per request size for last 30 days. Need a 10% sample trace from prod and synthetic reproduction harness that can drive continuous batching patterns (1000rps, 8-64 batch sizes, variable seq lengths).

2026-02-25 - Performance team (notes): Initial traces show KV accounts for 18-52% of used device memory depending on long context workloads. Activations have 10-40% variability due to batching and beam sizes. Observation: fragmentation on CUDA mempool is small but overall we lack an enforced soft-limit to protect activations during burst windows.

2026-03-02 - Design review: Agreed on slabs: weights (pinned, readonly), kv_slab (dynamic LFU-eviction candidate + compaction target), activation_slab (ephemeral, with headroom margin). Headroom policy: maintain min_headroom = max(activation_p95, kv_reserve_coeff * avg_kv) per tenant; global overcommit allowed up to 7% with graceful fallback. Need to quantify kv_reserve_coeff via experiments.

2026-03-05 - Connor Blake: Prototype notes — implemented a lightweight slab manager that reserves contiguous segments via cudaMemPool (where available) and falls back to cuMalloc+arena. Added accounting ledger per-tenant and per-model. Exposed metrics: slab_total_bytes, slab_used_bytes, slab_free_headroom, kv_evictions/sec, activation_peak_bytes.

2026-03-07 - QA: Synthetic stress run results attached in link below — compared baseline vs slabbed allocator. Key results: OOMs reduced from 9 to 1 over 24h mixed workload; median token latency +2.8%, tail p99 latency +6.5% during compaction windows. Need plan to reduce p99 impact (possible async compaction or throttle batches during compaction).

2026-03-09 - Security review request: new per-tenant ledger implies storing tenant memory usage in control plane metrics. Confirmed data is only usage counters and not customer content. SRE and Security need a brief sign-off for telemetry retention and export rules.

2026-03-10 - Next steps assigned: run parameter sweep for kv_reserve_coeff=[0.2,0.5,0.8] and min_headroom percentiles [p90,p95,p99] across 3 model families (Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B, OPT-30B) and report cost/latency trade-offs. Also prepare canary rollout plan for 2 Dedicated clusters and one Hosted cluster.

Follow-ups: 1) Investigate using compressed KV layout (4-bit packing) to increase effective KV capacity; 2) Explore integration with batching scheduler to avoid starting large batches when headroom < threshold.
notes:
Design trade-offs:
- Pros: predictable isolation between weight/kv/activations, fewer cross-tenant OOMs, simpler billing/telemetry for memory usage.
- Cons: added complexity in allocator, potential latency spikes during compaction/eviction, slightly lower GPU utilization in conservative configs.
Implementation options considered: a) full-page compaction using cuMemPool, b) opportunistic async eviction, c) purely soft-limits with eviction by priority. Team picked mixed approach (async eviction + soft headroom + optional compaction in background) to balance latency and memory efficiency.
Instrumentation plan: add per-request snapshot of slab usage to traces to correlate with tail latency; expose per-tenant headroom alerts in Console with automated canary cutoff.
Rollout plan: feature-flag rollout -> internal perf clusters -> 2 Dedicated canaries (non-critical customers) -> gradual ramp with telemetry gates (OOM rate, p99 latency, throughput).
Risk remediation: fallback mode will disable slab enforcement and revert to current allocator; this path should be togglable without pod restarts for Dedicated infra.
